text: Finance didn't ask for a dashboard. They asked for a workbook they can manipulate themselves — open, re-sum with their own formulas, and sign off on before any number goes into the QBR package.

Their export flattens the fact table and three dimensions into one human-readable sheet, with real column names and real dates instead of surrogate keys — a shape built for how a spreadsheet actually works, not for a modeled star schema.

This export is static on purpose. Finance's whole job is signing off on a specific, frozen set of numbers for one specific quarter — a constantly refreshing connection would work against that, not for it.
Next lesson builds the real workbook: a Power Query import, a PivotTable, and the formula that totals one specific quarter for Finance to check.
